interpretation: A final accepted charged particle is excluded from NCH_FINAL_STRONG_EM_V1 only when its explicit PYTHIA mother graph contains an actual weak-decay transition under weak_decay_transition_pythia_status_v1. Merely being, or descending through a same-particle copy of, a species in this registry is not sufficient.

transition_rule.parent_requirement: The parent has negative PYTHIA status and is a registered weak parent.
transition_rule.child_requirement: The child has absolute PYTHIA status 91 through 97, the documented decay-product statuses.
transition_rule.same_particle_links: Edges whose parent and child have the same absolute PDG ID are copy, recoil, or oscillation links and are traversed but are not themselves classified as weak decays.
transition_rule.excluded_statuses: Absolute status 99 is a Bose-Einstein momentum-shift copy and is not a decay transition.

open_heavy_rule: For conventional positive hadron PDG codes, classify the particle as an open-heavy weak parent when the tens, hundreds, or thousands quark digit is 4 or 5.
known_limitations: Classification follows explicit generator ancestry and therefore depends on preserved mother links.
The transition classification is tied to the documented PYTHIA 8.315 event-record status convention; a generator or status-convention change requires a new rule version.
All heavy-hadron decays are disabled in the canonical sample, so heavy-decay charged daughters are absent even though heavy parents remain in the exclusion rule.
This is a generator-level robustness counter, not an experimental primary-particle definition.
